record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that every (n, d, lambda')-graph with d/lambda' >= C contains a Hamilton cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9 (Krivelevich-Sudakov [91]). There exists an absolute constant C > 0 such that any (n, d, λ′)-graph with d/λ′ ≥ C contains a Hamilton cycle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph is a $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices whose adjacency matrix has the property that every eigenvalue other than $d$ has absolute value at most $\lambda$. A Hamilton cycle in a graph is a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that every $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph satisfying $d/\lambda \geq C$ contains a Hamilton cycle.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was resolved by Draganić, Montgomery, Munhá Correia, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov (2024), who proved that there is a constant C such that every C-expander is Hamiltonian, which implies the Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture on (n,d,λ)-graphs. Earlier partial progress was made by Glock, Munhá Correia, and Sudakov (2023).

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonicity of expanders: optimal bounds and applications
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a constant C > 0 for which every C-expander is Hamiltonian, which in particular implies the well-known conjecture of Krivelevich and Sudakov from 2003 on Hamilton cycles in (n,d,λ)-graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The Krivelevich-Sudakov conjecture on Hamilton cycles in (n,d,λ)-graphs is resolved.

status_evidence.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Settled the conjecture when d is at least a small power of n, and improved the general bound to λ ≤ d/C(log n)^{1/3}.
status_evidence.claim: Significant partial progress prior to the full resolution.
